name: No Poverty
description: End poverty in all its forms everywhere.
semantic_profile: This goal focuses on permanently reducing poverty by improving the living conditions, economic security and resilience of people experiencing deprivation or social exclusion. Projects aligned with this goal primarily aim to increase household income, expand access to social protection, strengthen livelihoods, improve financial resilience, reduce vulnerability to economic or environmental shocks, and ensure access to essential services such as housing, healthcare, education and basic infrastructure. Typical interventions include poverty alleviation programmes, income generation initiatives, financial inclusion, microfinance, social welfare systems, employment access for vulnerable populations, affordable housing, community development, social safety nets and inclusive local development. The intended outcome is a measurable reduction in poverty and socioeconomic vulnerability. While employment, education or healthcare may contribute to poverty reduction, they are considered supporting mechanisms rather than the primary objective. This goal is distinguished from SDG 8 because economic growth is only relevant when it directly improves the living conditions of disadvantaged populations, and from SDG 10 because the emphasis is on reducing poverty rather than reducing inequality.

name: Zero Hunger
description: End hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture.
semantic_profile: This goal focuses on ensuring that all people have reliable access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food while promoting sustainable and resilient agricultural systems. Projects aligned with this goal improve food security, eliminate hunger, address malnutrition, strengthen agricultural productivity, support farmers, improve food systems and increase the sustainability of crop, livestock, fisheries and aquaculture production. Typical activities include sustainable agriculture, regenerative farming, climate-smart agriculture, irrigation systems, agricultural technology, soil management, food storage, food supply chains, nutrition programmes, school feeding, agricultural research, seed improvement, rural food production and reducing food loss and waste. The intended outcome is improved food availability, nutrition or agricultural sustainability. Although projects may include innovation, logistics, productivity or rural development, these concepts are only relevant when directly related to food production, nutrition or agriculture. This goal should not be associated with generic industrial productivity, business competitiveness, digital innovation or non-agricultural supply chains, which belong primarily to SDGs 8 or 9.

name: Good Health and Well-being
description: Ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages.
semantic_profile: This goal focuses on improving physical and mental health, preventing disease, reducing mortality and ensuring equitable access to quality healthcare throughout every stage of life. Projects aligned with this goal strengthen healthcare systems, improve medical services, expand universal health coverage, promote disease prevention, improve maternal and child health, support healthy ageing, enhance mental health services and increase public health resilience. Typical interventions include hospitals, clinics, telemedicine, vaccination campaigns, medical research, health workforce development, emergency preparedness, health information systems, rehabilitation, pharmaceuticals, diagnostics, preventive medicine, nutrition programmes directly addressing health outcomes and health promotion initiatives. The intended outcome is improved health status, reduced illness, increased life expectancy or improved access to healthcare services. Although water, sanitation, nutrition or education may contribute to health outcomes, projects primarily addressing water infrastructure, educational systems or poverty reduction should instead align with SDGs 6, 4 or 1 respectively. Health is the principal objective rather than a secondary benefit.

name: Quality Education
description: Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all.
semantic_profile: This goal focuses on enabling people to acquire knowledge, competencies and lifelong learning opportunities through accessible, inclusive and high-quality education systems. Projects aligned with this goal improve formal education, non-formal education, lifelong learning, literacy, numeracy, digital literacy, higher education, vocational education, teacher training, curriculum development, educational inclusion and equal access to learning opportunities. Typical interventions include schools, universities, educational institutions, learning platforms, educational technology, scholarships, open education, special education, adult education, early childhood education and professional education programmes where learning itself is the principal outcome. Workforce training contributes to this goal when its primary purpose is education, skills acquisition or lifelong learning rather than employment creation or business competitiveness. Educational institutions, students, teachers, curricula and learning outcomes are central concepts. This goal is distinguished from SDG 8 because education is considered an end in itself rather than a means to economic growth, and from SDG 9 because technological innovation is relevant only when it directly improves teaching, learning or educational accessibility.

name: Gender Equality
description: Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls.
semantic_profile: This goal focuses on eliminating discrimination, barriers and inequalities affecting women and girls while ensuring equal rights, opportunities, participation and empowerment across all aspects of society. Projects aligned with this goal promote gender equality in education, employment, leadership, political participation, economic participation, entrepreneurship, healthcare, digital access and decision-making. Typical interventions include women's economic empowerment, gender-responsive policies, equal pay initiatives, prevention of gender-based violence, reproductive health and rights, financial inclusion for women, girls' education, leadership development, workplace equality, diversity and inclusion programmes, legal protection, representation and elimination of harmful practices. The intended outcome is increased gender equality and empowerment rather than general social inclusion. While women may benefit from projects in any sector, this goal applies when reducing gender disparities or advancing women's rights is the primary objective. It is distinguished from SDG 10 because the focus is specifically on gender-based inequalities rather than broader socioeconomic inequalities affecting multiple population groups.

name: Clean Water and Sanitation
description: Ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all.
semantic_profile: This goal focuses on ensuring universal access to safe drinking water, sanitation, hygiene and sustainable management of freshwater resources. Projects aligned with this goal improve water supply systems, drinking water quality, wastewater treatment, sanitation infrastructure, hygiene services, integrated water resource management, water conservation and protection of freshwater ecosystems. Typical interventions include water treatment plants, pipelines, wells, desalination, groundwater management, sewage systems, wastewater recycling, flood management, water monitoring, irrigation efficiency where water sustainability is the principal objective, watershed restoration, WASH programmes and sustainable freshwater governance. The intended outcome is improved access to water, sanitation or sustainable management of water resources. Although clean water contributes to public health, projects primarily addressing healthcare services or disease treatment belong to SDG 3. Likewise, agricultural irrigation belongs here only when water resource management is the principal objective rather than agricultural productivity.

name: Affordable and Clean Energy
description: Ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all.
semantic_profile: This goal focuses on expanding access to modern, affordable and sustainable energy while accelerating the transition toward cleaner energy systems. Projects aligned with this goal develop renewable energy generation, electricity access, energy infrastructure, energy storage, smart grids, clean cooking technologies and energy efficiency across buildings, transport and industry. Typical interventions include solar energy, wind power, hydropower, geothermal energy, battery systems, rural electrification, grid modernization, distributed energy systems, hydrogen technologies, electrification, energy management systems and low-carbon energy infrastructure. The intended outcome is improved availability, affordability, reliability or sustainability of energy services. Although renewable energy contributes to climate mitigation, projects whose principal objective is reducing greenhouse gas emissions or climate adaptation belong primarily to SDG 13. This goal is specifically concerned with energy production, distribution, access and efficiency rather than broader environmental sustainability.

name: Decent Work and Economic Growth
description: Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all.
semantic_profile: This goal focuses on creating sustainable economic opportunities through employment, entrepreneurship, enterprise development and inclusive economic growth. Projects aligned with this goal strengthen labour markets, create decent jobs, support entrepreneurs, develop micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs and SMEs), improve business competitiveness, expand productive employment, increase labour productivity and foster resilient local and national economies. Typical interventions include business incubation, startup acceleration, SME support programmes, entrepreneurship training, workforce development linked to employability, vocational training aimed at labour market participation, employment services, financial inclusion for businesses, sustainable tourism development, local economic development, responsible business practices, labour rights, workplace safety and productivity improvement. The intended outcome is measurable economic growth, business development, enterprise competitiveness, job creation, higher employment or improved quality of work. Training is relevant only when it serves employment or enterprise development rather than education itself. Innovation contributes to this goal when it strengthens businesses or economic performance, whereas projects primarily advancing research, industrial technology, digital infrastructure or technological innovation belong to SDG 9. Economic outcomes are the defining characteristic of this goal.

name: Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure
description: Build resilient infrastructure, promote inclusive and sustainable industrialization and foster innovation.
semantic_profile: This goal focuses on strengthening industrial capacity, technological innovation, scientific research and resilient infrastructure that enable sustainable economic development. Projects aligned with this goal develop new technologies, industrial processes, research capabilities, engineering solutions, manufacturing systems, digital transformation, advanced production methods and critical infrastructure. Typical interventions include research and development (R&D), technology transfer, digital technologies, artificial intelligence, robotics, automation, advanced manufacturing, Industry 4.0, industrial modernization, engineering, broadband infrastructure, transport infrastructure, logistics systems, laboratories, innovation ecosystems, technology commercialization, science parks, startup innovation, product development and industrial competitiveness. The intended outcome is technological advancement, stronger industrial capability, resilient infrastructure or innovation capacity. Innovation itself is the principal objective rather than simply a tool supporting another sector. Projects whose primary purpose is creating jobs belong to SDG 8, educational programmes belong to SDG 4, and environmental sustainability initiatives belong to SDGs 12, 13, 14 or 15 unless innovation or infrastructure development is the central outcome.

name: Reduced Inequalities
description: Reduce inequality within and among countries.
semantic_profile: This goal focuses on reducing social, economic and political inequalities by ensuring equitable opportunities, inclusion and participation for all people regardless of income, disability, age, ethnicity, migration status or other characteristics. Projects aligned with this goal remove systemic barriers, improve accessibility, promote equal participation, reduce discrimination and increase inclusion of disadvantaged or marginalized populations. Typical interventions include disability inclusion, accessible services, inclusive employment, refugee and migrant integration, social inclusion programmes, equal opportunity initiatives, inclusive public policies, financial inclusion, anti-discrimination measures, equitable access to education, healthcare and digital services, social protection for vulnerable groups and inclusive governance. The intended outcome is a measurable reduction in inequalities or exclusion rather than poverty reduction alone. While many projects benefit vulnerable populations, this goal applies when reducing disparities between groups is the principal objective. It is distinguished from SDG 1, which focuses specifically on poverty, and SDG 5, which focuses specifically on gender equality.

name: Sustainable Cities and Communities
description: Make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable.
semantic_profile: This goal focuses on improving the sustainability, resilience, safety and inclusiveness of cities, towns and human settlements. Projects aligned with this goal enhance urban environments, housing, mobility, public infrastructure and community resilience while improving quality of life for residents. Typical interventions include sustainable urban planning, affordable housing, smart cities, public transport, active mobility, cycling infrastructure, pedestrian infrastructure, green buildings, urban regeneration, disaster resilience, public spaces, cultural heritage preservation, community facilities, municipal services, urban biodiversity, waste management at city level, air quality improvement and resilient local infrastructure. The intended outcome is a more sustainable and liveable built environment. Digital technologies, infrastructure and innovation contribute only when they directly improve urban systems or communities. This goal differs from SDG 9 because the emphasis is on cities and communities rather than industrial or technological innovation, and from SDG 13 because climate resilience is considered within the context of human settlements.

name: Responsible Consumption and Production
description: Ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns.
semantic_profile: This goal focuses on transforming how products, materials and natural resources are produced, consumed and managed throughout their life cycle. Projects aligned with this goal improve resource efficiency, reduce waste, promote circular economy principles and encourage sustainable production and consumption practices across industries and society. Typical interventions include recycling systems, reuse strategies, remanufacturing, eco-design, sustainable product development, life-cycle assessment, industrial ecology, sustainable procurement, responsible sourcing, sustainable supply chains, waste prevention, food waste reduction, packaging optimization, cleaner production processes, material efficiency, environmental management systems, product stewardship and circular business models. The intended outcome is reduced environmental impact through more sustainable resource use rather than technological innovation itself. Innovation contributes to this goal when it enables circularity, waste reduction or sustainable production. Projects primarily developing new technologies without a sustainability objective belong to SDG 9, while projects focused primarily on climate mitigation belong to SDG 13.

name: Climate Action
description: Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts.
semantic_profile: This goal focuses on mitigating climate change, adapting to its impacts and strengthening resilience to climate-related risks. Projects aligned with this goal reduce greenhouse gas emissions, accelerate decarbonization, improve climate adaptation, strengthen disaster risk reduction and integrate climate considerations into public policies, business strategies and infrastructure planning. Typical interventions include carbon reduction, net-zero strategies, renewable energy transition where the principal objective is emissions reduction, climate adaptation planning, carbon accounting, greenhouse gas monitoring, climate finance, resilience planning, nature-based climate adaptation, disaster preparedness, early warning systems, climate governance, climate education, carbon capture, emissions reporting and climate risk assessment. The intended outcome is measurable progress in addressing climate change through mitigation, adaptation or resilience. Environmental projects belong to this goal only when climate change is the primary focus. Biodiversity conservation, ecosystem restoration, forestry, agriculture or marine conservation should instead align with SDGs 15, 2 or 14 unless their principal objective is climate mitigation or adaptation.

name: Life Below Water
description: Conserve and sustainably use the oceans, seas and marine resources for sustainable development.
semantic_profile: This goal focuses on protecting marine ecosystems and ensuring the sustainable use of oceans, seas and coastal resources. Projects aligned with this goal conserve marine biodiversity, improve ocean health, restore coastal habitats and promote sustainable management of marine resources. Typical interventions include marine conservation, sustainable fisheries, sustainable aquaculture, coral reef restoration, marine protected areas, blue economy initiatives, coastal ecosystem management, marine biodiversity monitoring, ocean observation, reduction of marine pollution, plastic pollution prevention, sustainable seafood, coastal resilience, estuary restoration, seagrass conservation, mangrove restoration, marine spatial planning and sustainable ocean governance. The intended outcome is healthier marine ecosystems and sustainable use of ocean resources. Water-related projects focused on freshwater systems belong to SDG 6, while terrestrial biodiversity and forests belong to SDG 15. Climate-related marine projects should only align with SDG 13 when climate mitigation or adaptation is the principal objective rather than marine ecosystem conservation itself.

name: Life on Land
description: Protect, restore and promote sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, sustainably manage forests, combat desertification, and halt and reverse land degradation and halt biodiversity loss.
semantic_profile: This goal focuses on conserving, restoring and sustainably managing terrestrial ecosystems, biodiversity and natural habitats. Projects aligned with this goal protect forests, wildlife, soils and ecosystems while restoring degraded landscapes and preventing biodiversity loss. Typical interventions include reforestation, afforestation, forest management, habitat restoration, ecosystem restoration, biodiversity conservation, wildlife protection, ecological restoration, protected areas, conservation planning, sustainable forestry, soil conservation, land restoration, desertification prevention, invasive species management, ecological connectivity, nature restoration, ecosystem monitoring and sustainable land management. The intended outcome is healthier terrestrial ecosystems, improved biodiversity and sustainable management of natural land resources. Climate benefits may occur as a co-benefit, but projects belong to this goal when ecosystem conservation or biodiversity protection is the primary objective. Marine ecosystems belong to SDG 14, while climate mitigation strategies primarily focused on greenhouse gas emissions belong to SDG 13.

name: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
description: Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels.
semantic_profile: This goal focuses on strengthening governance, justice, public institutions and the rule of law to build peaceful, accountable and inclusive societies. Projects aligned with this goal improve institutional effectiveness, transparency, accountability, democratic participation, public administration, legal systems, anti-corruption measures, human rights protection and access to justice. Typical interventions include judicial reform, public sector modernization, digital government, open government, civic participation, electoral processes, institutional capacity, public accountability, regulatory quality, conflict prevention, peacebuilding, mediation, community safety, human rights, legal empowerment, public policy, public service delivery, ethics, compliance, law enforcement reform and institutional resilience. The intended outcome is stronger institutions, better governance or greater public trust. Digital technologies, training or innovation contribute to this goal only when they strengthen governance or justice systems. Projects focused primarily on business development, education or international cooperation belong instead to SDGs 8, 4 or 17.

name: Partnerships for the Goals
description: Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the Global Partnership for Sustainable Development.
semantic_profile: This goal focuses exclusively on establishing, strengthening and coordinating partnerships that enable sustainable development through collaboration between multiple organizations, sectors, countries or stakeholder groups. Projects aligned with this goal create or reinforce formal cooperation mechanisms, strategic alliances, international partnerships, public-private partnerships, multi-stakeholder initiatives, development cooperation programmes, global networks, cross-sector collaboration, intergovernmental cooperation, donor coordination, joint implementation frameworks, partnership governance, consortium-based projects, collaborative financing, international resource mobilization and coordinated implementation of sustainable development objectives. Typical evidence includes partnerships between governments, universities, companies, NGOs, research organisations, international agencies or civil society working together under a common governance structure. Capacity building, knowledge sharing, technology transfer, innovation, research, digital transformation or training contribute to this goal only when they are explicitly carried out through collaborative partnership mechanisms. Projects undertaken by a single organisation, even if they include innovation, training, sustainability or business support, should not align with this goal unless partnerships themselves are a principal objective and an essential implementation mechanism. The defining characteristic of this goal is collaboration between independent actors rather than the thematic content of the project itself.
